questions.topic: Ch18 Enthalpy of Reaction Calculation
questions.question: Using standard BDE tables for Chapter 18 chemical transformations, how is the reaction enthalpy (ΔH°rxn) calculated?

options.label: D
options.text: ΔH°rxn = Σ(BDE of all bonds broken in reactants) - Σ(BDE of all bonds formed in products) for Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: ΔH°rxn = Σ(BDE of all bonds broken in reactants) - Σ(BDE of all bonds formed in products) for Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: Enthalpy change equals the energy invested to homolytically break reactant bonds minus energy released forming product bonds.

questions.topic: Ch18 Gibbs Free Energy Equilibrium Relation
questions.question: What exact mathematical equation relates standard Gibbs free energy (ΔG°) to the equilibrium constant (Keq) in Chapter 18?

options.label: A
options.text: ΔG° = -RT ln(Keq) or Keq = exp(-ΔG° / RT) (where R = 8.314 J/mol·K and T is in Kelvin) for Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: ΔG° = -RT ln(Keq) or Keq = exp(-ΔG° / RT) (where R = 8.314 J/mol·K and T is in Kelvin) for Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: The fundamental thermodynamic relationship connects standard free energy to the equilibrium constant Keq.

questions.topic: Ch18 Arrhenius Equation Activation Energy
questions.question: According to the Arrhenius equation k = A exp(-Ea/RT), how does a 10 kJ/mol increase in Ea affect the rate constant k in Chapter 18?

options.label: A
options.text: It decreases the rate constant k by a factor of ~55 at 298 K (k_new = k_old × e^(-10000 / 2478) ≈ 0.018 × k_old) in Chapter 18.

options.label: B
options.text: It increases the rate constant by 10 fold.

options.label: C
options.text: It has zero effect on the rate constant.

questions.correct_answer: It decreases the rate constant k by a factor of ~55 at 298 K (k_new = k_old × e^(-10000 / 2478) ≈ 0.018 × k_old) in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: Higher activation energy exponentially suppresses the fraction of molecular collisions possessing sufficient kinetic energy to react.

questions.topic: Ch18 Primary Kinetic Isotope Effect Diagnostic
questions.question: In Chapter 18 mechanistic investigations, what primary deuterium isotope effect (k_H / k_D) confirms C-H cleavage in the RDS?

options.label: B
options.text: A primary isotope effect of k_H / k_D between 5.0 and 8.0 at 25°C in Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: A primary isotope effect of k_H / k_D between 5.0 and 8.0 at 25°C in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: Primary KIE values of 5–8 indicate that the zero-point vibrational energy of the C-H bond is lost in the rate-determining transition state.

questions.topic: Ch18 Secondary Kinetic Isotope Effect Analysis
questions.question: In Chapter 18 substitution reactions, what does a normal secondary KIE (k_H / k_D = 1.15 to 1.25) indicate?

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-H bond.

options.label: C
options.text: An sp³ (tetrahedral) to sp² (planar carbocation) hybridization change in the rate-determining step in Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: An sp³ (tetrahedral) to sp² (planar carbocation) hybridization change in the rate-determining step in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: Rehybridization from sp³ to sp² loosens out-of-plane bending vibrations, accelerating the lighter protium isotopologue (normal secondary KIE > 1).

questions.topic: Ch18 Eyring Transition State Theory Math
questions.question: According to transition state theory (Eyring equation), what thermodynamic quantity dictates reaction rate in Chapter 18?

options.label: B
options.text: The molecular weight of the solvent.

options.label: C
options.text: The overall reaction enthalpy ΔH°rxn exclusively.

options.label: D
options.text: The standard Gibbs free energy of activation (ΔG‡ = ΔH‡ - TΔS‡), where k = (k_B·T / h) exp(-ΔG‡ / RT) in Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: The standard Gibbs free energy of activation (ΔG‡ = ΔH‡ - TΔS‡), where k = (k_B·T / h) exp(-ΔG‡ / RT) in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: The free energy barrier ΔG‡ (including both activation enthalpy and activation entropy) controls the absolute rate constant.

questions.topic: Ch18 Activation Entropy (Delta S-Double Dagger) Interpretation
questions.question: What does a large negative activation entropy (ΔS‡ = -100 to -150 J/mol·K) signify for a Chapter 18 mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: A dissociative unimolecular step with ion formation.

options.label: B
options.text: An associative, highly ordered transition state where two or more molecules combine with severe loss of translational and rotational freedom in Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: An associative, highly ordered transition state where two or more molecules combine with severe loss of translational and rotational freedom in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: Large negative ΔS‡ values are diagnostic for bimolecular associative transition states (e.g., Diels-Alder, SN2).

questions.topic: Ch18 Hammond Postulate Reaction Coordinate Math
questions.question: In an endergonic elementary step (ΔG° > 0) in Chapter 18, how does the transition state location (x_TS) correlate with energy?

options.label: A
options.text: The transition state is at x_TS = 0.0.

options.label: B
options.text: The transition state occurs late along the reaction coordinate (x_TS > 0.5), structurally and energetically resembling the high-energy intermediate in Chapter 18.

options.label: D
options.text: The transition state does not exist.

questions.correct_answer: The transition state occurs late along the reaction coordinate (x_TS > 0.5), structurally and energetically resembling the high-energy intermediate in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: According to the Hammond postulate, endergonic steps have late transition states that closely mirror the adjacent high-energy intermediate.

questions.topic: Ch18 Kinetic vs Thermodynamic Ratio Math
questions.question: At 298 K, if two competing pathways differ in activation barrier by ΔΔG‡ = 11.4 kJ/mol in Chapter 18, what is the kinetic product ratio?

options.label: C
options.text: The faster pathway yields a 100:1 kinetic product ratio (k₁ / k₂ = exp(ΔΔG‡ / RT) = exp(11400 / 2478) ≈ 100) in Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: The faster pathway yields a 100:1 kinetic product ratio (k₁ / k₂ = exp(ΔΔG‡ / RT) = exp(11400 / 2478) ≈ 100) in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: A difference in activation barrier of 11.4 kJ/mol at 25°C produces a 100:1 kinetic selectivity ratio between competing pathways.

questions.topic: Ch18 Quantitative pKa and Delta G Connection
questions.question: What mathematical relationship connects the pKa difference (ΔpKa) in a Chapter 18 acid-base equilibrium to standard free energy (ΔG°)?

options.label: B
options.text: ΔG° = 2.303 RT × ΔpKa ≈ 5.7 kJ/mol × (pKa_reactant_acid - pKa_product_acid) at 298 K in Chapter 18.

questions.correct_answer: ΔG° = 2.303 RT × ΔpKa ≈ 5.7 kJ/mol × (pKa_reactant_acid - pKa_product_acid) at 298 K in Chapter 18.
questions.explanation: Each unit difference in pKa (factor of 10 in Ka) corresponds to 2.303 RT ≈ 5.7 kJ/mol of free energy at 25°C.

questions.question: What exact mathematical equation relates standard Gibbs free energy (ΔG°) to the equilibrium constant (Keq) in Chapter 18?

questions.topic: Ch18 Primary Kinetic Isotope Effect Diagnostic
questions.question: In Chapter 18 mechanistic investigations, what primary deuterium isotope effect (k_H / k_D) confirms C-H cleavage in the RDS?

questions.topic: Ch18 Secondary Kinetic Isotope Effect Analysis
questions.question: In Chapter 18 substitution reactions, what does a normal secondary KIE (k_H / k_D = 1.15 to 1.25) indicate?

questions.topic: Ch18 Eyring Transition State Theory Math

options.text: The standard Gibbs free energy of activation (ΔG‡ = ΔH‡ - TΔS‡), where k = (k_B·T / h) exp(-ΔG‡ / RT) in Chapter 18.

options.label: B

questions.explanation: The free energy barrier ΔG‡ (including both activation enthalpy and activation entropy) controls the absolute rate constant.
